blocks.text: 1. Late Interaction Models

blocks.alt: Token-level embeddings go through late interaction scoring to produce a relevance score

blocks.text: ColBERT's closing recap pointed forward to this next topic. Late Interaction Models steps back to name the general category that ColBERT belongs to, covering this family of techniques in broader depth.
It names that general category directly, along with the related variants that share the same underlying idea.
2. From One Example To A Whole Category
ColBERT was one specific, well known implementation of a broader idea.
Late interaction models is the name for that broader category.

blocks.text: 3. Defining The Late Interaction Principle

blocks.alt: Early interaction as in cross encoders is compared against late interaction as in ColBERT

blocks.text: ColBERT sits at neither extreme: any model that embeds independently but compares at a fine grained level qualifies as a late interaction model.
The defining trait is postponing interaction, not the specific scoring formula used.
4. Variations On The Scoring Formula

blocks.alt: MaxSim and sum of max are scoring formula variants

blocks.text: ColBERT's MaxSim scoring mechanism is one specific way to combine token level similarities.
Other late interaction models can use different aggregation formulas over the same underlying token embeddings.
5. Indexing Challenges For Late Interaction

blocks.alt: Many token vectors require complex indexing

blocks.text: ColBERT's storage cost comes from keeping a full set of token level vectors around, and indexing many token vectors per chunk complicates standard vector database indexing.
Specialized indexing structures are often needed to keep late interaction models searchable at scale.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A standard vector index built for one vector per chunk does not directly support storing and searching dozens of token vectors per chunk, so purpose built indexing structures are needed instead.

blocks.text: 6. Compression Techniques For Late Interaction

blocks.alt: Token vectors are compressed into a smaller footprint

blocks.text: Quantization, as covered in Compression, applies here too: token level vectors can be quantized just like whole chunk vectors.
Compression helps offset the extra storage cost that is inherent to this family of models.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Applying quantization to token level embeddings reduces the storage multiplier that late interaction models otherwise carry compared to standard bi-encoders, making the approach more practical at scale.

blocks.text: 7. Where This Technique Sits In Practice

blocks.alt: Bi-encoder gives speed, late interaction sits in the middle, cross encoder gives accuracy

blocks.text: In the two stage pipeline covered under Why Re-Ranking, late interaction models can serve as either a fast first stage or a refined re-ranking stage.
Their exact placement depends on how well their indexing has been optimized.
8. Ongoing Research Direction
Late interaction models remain an active area of research and improvement.
New variants continue emerging that push accuracy and efficiency further.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When A Late Interaction Model Fits A Pipeline

blocks.alt: Needing token-level precision at scale points toward a late interaction model

blocks.text: Systems with specialized indexing support and a need for strong accuracy suit this family well.
Simple pipelines without specialized infrastructure may prefer a plain bi-encoder or cross encoder instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below compares two different aggregation formulas over the same token embeddings.

code.content:
def fake_token_embed(token):
    return (len(token), sum(ord(c) for c in token) % 100)

def cosine_like_similarity(v1, v2):
    dot = sum(a * b for a, b in zip(v1, v2))
    mag1 = sum(a * a for a in v1) ** 0.5
    mag2 = sum(a * a for a in v2) ** 0.5
    return dot / (mag1 * mag2) if mag1 and mag2 else 0

def maxsim_aggregation(query_embeddings, chunk_embeddings):
    # one way to aggregate token level similarities
    return sum(max(cosine_like_similarity(q, c) for c in chunk_embeddings) for q in query_embeddings)

def average_aggregation(query_embeddings, chunk_embeddings):
    # an alternative aggregation formula over the same token embeddings
    total = 0
    for q in query_embeddings:
        scores = [cosine_like_similarity(q, c) for c in chunk_embeddings]
        total += sum(scores) / len(scores)
    return total

query_tokens = "refund policy".split()
chunk_tokens = "our refund policy allows returns within thirty days".split()

query_embeddings = [fake_token_embed(t) for t in query_tokens]
chunk_embeddings = [fake_token_embed(t) for t in chunk_tokens]

print(f"MaxSim aggregation score: {maxsim_aggregation(query_embeddings, chunk_embeddings):.3f}")
print(f"Average aggregation score: {average_aggregation(query_embeddings, chunk_embeddings):.3f}")
print("\nBoth formulas operate on the same token level embeddings,")
print("just aggregating them differently.")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows two different aggregation formulas producing different final scores from the exact same underlying token embeddings.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Assuming late interaction models are synonymous with ColBERT rather than a broader category.
Underestimating the specialized indexing infrastructure this family of models typically requires.
Ignoring compression options that could offset the extra storage cost of token level vectors.
Deploying a late interaction model without infrastructure that can actually support its indexing needs.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Late interaction models name the broader category that ColBERT is one specific implementation of.
The defining trait is postponing interaction until after independent embedding, not a fixed formula.
MaxSim is one specific aggregation formula; other late interaction models can use different ones.
Indexing many token vectors per chunk complicates standard vector database indexing.
Specialized indexing structures are often needed to keep this family searchable at scale.
Token level vectors can be quantized to offset their extra storage cost.
This family can serve as either a fast first stage or a refined re-ranking stage.
Late interaction models remain an active area of ongoing research and improvement.
